newsitem.title: USA: Xerox prepared to sell Talegen in pieces.
newsitem.headline: Xerox prepared to sell Talegen in pieces.

text.p: Xerox Corp, whose planned sale of its Talegen insurance unit to Kohlberg Kravis Roberts & Co collapsed, said on Thursday it now believes the business is more likely to sell in several pieces rather than as a whole.

Xerox, which scheduled a conference call with analysts for 1000 EDT/1400 GMT today, still believes it can sell Talegen but said it could take until the end of 1997 before it is completely out of the business.

A Xerox spokesman said the company has asked its financial adviser, Morgan Stanley, "to try to structure a sale in any way that makes the best sense for Xerox -- and that could be a piece at a time, which we think is more likely now than an entire, one big sale like we had with KKR."
He said of Talegen, "We think it's more likely now that it will be sold in pieces." The business consists of five different units.
He added, "We still think we can get at least the amount we had agreed to with KKR -- the $2.7 billion."
He declined comment on the reason the KKR deal collapsed.
